relatedSnapshot.title: Failed pre-warmed mailbox connects count as in-flight OAuth sessions for 48h, so retries stall and orders sit in requires_attention
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Intercom source

<url:app.intercom.com>

## Bounded conversation context

Customer-initiated chat from Name 1 (<email>), workspace <workspace-slug> (organization <uuid>), 2026-09-24 \~22:54 UTC. Opened with "i need help with the cold email agent", said "setup inboxes", asked how long provisioning takes, then sent a screenshot of the Cold Email Agent Email Accounts area and said "i have this screen showing" / "trying to launch the campaigns tonight". Fin answered from help-centre articles (provisioning takes 15-30 min, up to \~1 hour) and escalated to a human. Agent Ellaine Fuente replied "I see your inboxes are still having issues. I will look into this".

## Testable claim

A pre-warmed inbox order whose mailbox OAuth connect fails with the mail provider's rate-limit response is never retried again: recordConnectionFailure marks the newest OAuth session 'failed', and the reconcile-domain-orders retry loop skips a mailbox whenever its newest session status is neither 'expired' nor 'completed', so the mailboxes stay disconnected and the order stays in requires_attention indefinitely. For this order: 6 pre-warmed domains and 18 mailbox rows were created, 0 of 18 connected, and no connect attempt has run since 2026-09-24T15:20:24Z.

## Known signature

mail_inbox.status='error', connected=false, connection_error "Mailbox OAuth connection threw an exception: Rate limit exceeded, please try again later." Started: 2026-09-24T12:04:25Z.

## Impact for this customer

Paid order <uuid> (6 domains x 3 pre-warmed inboxes) is unusable and the UI shows an endless "Provisioning in progress"; the customer cannot launch campaigns.

relatedSnapshot.title: Reconcile retry gate treats a failed mailbox OAuth session as in flight for 48h, so pre-warmed inbox retries stall
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

A mailbox whose OAuth connect to the mail provider fails is retried at a two-day cadence instead of every 30 minutes, because the provisioning reconcile loop counts the failure's own OAuth session as work still in flight. Pre-warmed inboxes stay in Error and their orders sit in `requires_attention`, so customers who paid for inboxes cannot send for days and the UI eventually reports the retry budget as exhausted.

## Problem

A workspace buys pre-warmed inboxes. The domains provision, the mailbox rows are created, and then nothing completes: Email Accounts shows the mailboxes in Error, the order banner says provisioning requires attention, and later "N mailboxes could not be retried / Retry budget exhausted. Contact support to re-run these exports." No customer action changes it; Reconnect re-enters the same failing path.

## Root cause

`recordConnectionFailure` (`apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/campaign/workspaces/oauth-connection-failure.ts`) defaults to `sessionStatus: 'failed'` and marks the newest `cea_oauth_sessions` row for the mailbox+order failed. Both connect-failure shapes reach it from `processConnectOAuth`'s `connect-mailbox-oauth` step (`apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/campaign/workspaces/process-connect-oauth.ts`): a `status === 'failed'` result and a thrown `ApiClientError` (for example the provider's HTTP 429 "Rate limit exceeded, please try again later.").

`reconcileDomainOrdersCron` (`apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/billing/reconcile-domain-orders-cron.ts`, `find-orders-requiring-attention` loop, skip predicate around l.1168–1185) then reads the newest session with `getOAuthSessionForOrderAndEmail` and `continue`s whenever that session is younger than `SESSION_VALIDITY_HOURS` (48) and its status is neither `expired` nor `completed`, on the assumption that `pollOAuthSession` is still polling it. Nothing polls an order-scoped `failed` session: `pollOAuthSession` exits on `failed`, and `reconcileOAuthSessionsCron` filters `order_id IS NULL`. The mailbox is therefore not attempted again until the session crosses the 48-hour cutoff, at which point the loop's next branch marks it expired and retries. While retry-eligible failed inboxes remain the loop also never finalizes the order, so it stays in `requires_attention` with `completed_at` null; after 24 cycles `finalizeUnfulfillableOrderAfterRetries` stops retrying, and on the Autumn path that finalization releases the seats without refunding them.

## Blast radius

13 orders across 13 organizations, holding 95 mailboxes currently behind the gate (newest session `failed` and younger than the 48-hour cutoff), counted 2026-09-24T23:55Z with:

```
WITH latest AS (SELECT DISTINCT ON (order_id, email) order_id, email, status, created_at
  FROM cea_oauth_sessions WHERE order_id IS NOT NULL ORDER BY order_id, email, created_at DESC)
SELECT count(DISTINCT l.order_id), count(DISTINCT o.organization_id), count(*)
FROM latest l JOIN domain_purchase_order o ON o.id = l.order_id
WHERE l.status='failed' AND o.status='requires_attention' AND o.completed_at IS NULL
  AND l.created_at > now() - interval '48 hours'
```

One of the 13 has zero inboxes delivered; the other 12 are partially provisioned (3–24 inboxes) and cycling. Widening the query without the 48-hour condition returns 16 orders / 16 organizations / 125 mailboxes, but 6 of those hold newest failed sessions months old and are excluded from the retry loop by the latest-actionable-order filter, so they are not evidence for this gate. Memberships are single-user workspaces; distinct affected users were not counted separately.

## Proposed fix

Treat terminal session statuses as not in flight in the reconcile gate, so a mailbox whose connect failed is retried on the next pass, and give the connect step a bounded backoff for provider throttling so a 429 does not consume the mailbox's 24-attempt budget at a two-day cadence.

## What's included

The gate predicate and the retry cadence for order-scoped OAuth sessions. Not included: the separate reconnect paths that never resolve a provider mailbox id (ENG-13178), the stale `mail_domain` claim class (ENG-13213), and the Autumn decision about refunding seats that were never connected. ENG-14185's recorded "burning that budget over weeks" footprint is this gate's effect and should be cross-linked rather than merged.

## Regression seam

Reconcile pass over a `requires_attention` order whose mailbox's newest session is in `failed` status. Red before: no `retry-connect-oauth-` step runs and the inbox is untouched for the next 48 hours. Green after: the `failed` session does not block the pass and the attempted connect runs on that pass.

## Done when

* A mailbox whose newest session is `failed` is attempted again on the next reconcile pass instead of after 48 hours.
* A throttled connect does not consume one of the 24 retry attempts per two-day cycle.
* A regression test proves red-before/green-after at the seam above.

## Reports

* ENG-14249

relatedSnapshot.title: ColdMailReseller pre-warmed inboxes stuck in Error: reconnect sends mailboxId=undefined ("Mailbox not found")
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Pre-warmed mailboxes provisioned through ColdMailReseller get stuck in an Error state and cannot send, because no reconnect path resolves a mailbox id the provider will accept.

## Problem

When a ColdMailReseller pre-warmed inbox disconnects or needs reconnecting, the account-error reconnect flow fires with `mailboxId: providerId ?? undefined`. These inboxes have `mail_inbox.provider_id = NULL`, so the provider receives `mailboxId=undefined` and the OAuth connect returns "Mailbox not found", leaving the inbox permanently in Error.

## Root cause

`apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/campaign/workspaces/process-account-error-reconnect.ts` invokes `processConnectOAuth` with `mailboxId: inboxLookup.providerId ?? undefined`. `processConnectOAuth` (`process-connect-oauth.ts`, `connect-mailbox-oauth` step) forwards that `mailboxId` to ColdMailReseller `POST /mailboxes/oauth` via `apps/web/lib/mail/providers/coldmailreseller/client.ts#connectMailboxOAuth`, which rejects it with "Mailbox not found". The inboxes have `mail_inbox.provider_id = NULL`, so the id is never resolved. The reconcile cron (`reconcile-domain-orders-cron.ts`) already looks up the mailbox from ColdMailReseller and passes `mailbox.id` correctly, so the resolution pattern exists.

The failing invariant is one gap across every entry point: no reconnect path resolves the mailbox id from ColdMailReseller before calling the provider. The webhook path forwards the stored `mail_inbox.provider_id`; the customer Reconnect action (`email-accounts.ts`, `triggerOAuthReconnect`) and the admin reconnect (`admin-domain-orders.ts`) both send `mailboxId: undefined`; `processConnectOAuth` never re-resolves. An inbox carrying a named but no-longer-valid id fails identically to one with a NULL id, which is why both counts below sit in this one class.

## Blast radius

5,762 inboxes across 444 organizations carry a `connection_error` containing "Mailbox not found" (query: `SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT organization_id) FROM mail_inbox WHERE connection_error ILIKE '%Mailbox not found%'`, counted 2026-09-24: 5,762 inboxes / 444 organizations, and 7,071 reconnect sessions across 461 organizations failed the same way in the 30 days to 2026-09-24; was 5,763 / 445 on 2026-09-23, 5,660 / 439 on 2026-09-22, 4,364 / 323 on 2026-09-10 and 294 / 39 on 2026-08-28). None of the 5,762 is connected now. 2,391 of them carry the exact `mailboxId=undefined` signature (and all of those have `provider_id IS NULL`); the larger 3,371 carry a named mailbox id and fail the same way. Named-id rows arrive in platform waves (2026-09-04 to 09-06 roughly 2,118 rows across 95+ organizations; 2026-09-19 to 09-20 roughly 1,148 rows across 103 organizations), so the shape is systematic rather than org-specific. A further 2,872 connected pre-warmed inboxes across 228 organizations sit at `provider_id IS NULL` and would fail the same way on their next reconnect.

## Proposed fix

Resolve the provider mailbox id before reconnecting: look up the mailbox from ColdMailReseller (as the reconcile cron already does) instead of passing `provider_id` or `undefined`, and backfill `provider_id` for the affected inboxes so they reconnect successfully.

## Done when

* No reconnect path hands ColdMailReseller an unresolved id: the webhook path stops forwarding the stored `provider_id` unresolved, the customer Reconnect and admin reconnect stop sending `undefined`, and both shapes (NULL `provider_id` and stale named id) reconnect successfully.
* The stuck inboxes are recovered or re-provisioned and resume sending.
* Provider accounts with no local `mail_inbox` row are covered too: Reconnect refuses them outright (`email-accounts.ts#triggerOAuthReconnect` throws PRECONDITION_FAILED "Only managed inboxes can be reconnected.") while their inbox entitlements are still consumed, so the backfill and re-provision step must create or link the missing rows, not only repair a NULL or stale `provider_id`.

## Reports

* ENG-13156
* ENG-13255
* ENG-13511
* ENG-14104
* ENG-14131
* ENG-14197 Customer report: all 15 pre-warmed inboxes stuck in Error; Reconnect returns Mailbox not found; campaigns cannot send
* ENG-14201 Customer report: 15 of 36 pre-warmed inboxes stuck in Error; Reconnect returns Mailbox not found and never clears the inbox

relatedSnapshot.title: Pre-warmed mailbox connect conflicts are retried to exhaustion and the unconnected seats stay billed after finalization
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Pre-warmed Done-For-You mailboxes that the mail provider already reports as owned by another workspace can never be connected, and the seats are billed anyway. Operators pay for inboxes that have never worked, and the orders they belong to are closed out without releasing the charge.

## Problem

An operator buys pre-warmed domains with three inboxes each. Some of the mailboxes in the assignment cannot be connected to the buyer's workspace, so those domains are left half-built: the domain is provisioned, its inboxes sit in an error state, and the order is eventually closed out with the seats still granted and still billed. There is no customer-side reconnect for a managed inbox in this state, and nothing in the finalization path releases the charge.

## Root cause

A permanent provider conflict is treated as a transient connect failure, and finalization releases no seats on Autumn accounts.

* `apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/billing/process-domain-purchase-order.ts`, `processDomainPurchaseOrder`: invokes `processConnectOAuth` per mailbox; on a failure result it logs and pushes `{success:false, error}` and continues, and the domain is later written as `partial` when any inbox did not connect.
* `apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/campaign/workspaces/process-connect-oauth.ts`, `processConnectOAuth`: surfaces the provider's failure text ("OAuth connection failed: account_exists - Account already exists in another workspace") and consumes retry budget.
* `apps/web/lib/mail/db/mail-repository.ts`: `MAX_INBOX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS = 24`, and `isEligibleForRetry: row.retryCount < MAX_INBOX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS`.
* `apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/billing/reconcile-domain-orders-cron.ts`, `reconcileDomainOrdersCron`: the `find-orders-requiring-attention` loop re-invokes the connect for every still-eligible failed inbox each cycle, so a conflict that can never succeed burns \~24 cycles over several weeks; once `eligibleForRetry.length === 0 && failedInboxes.length > 0` it calls `finalizeUnfulfillableOrderAfterRetries`.
* `apps/web/lib/billing/order-finalization.ts`, `finalizeUnfulfillableOrderAfterRetries`: for an order with provisioned items it writes `status: 'requires_attention'`, `completedAt` and `errorDetails.retriesExhausted = true`, and calls `applyManagedDomainCancellationAdjustment` only inside `if (billingProvider === 'whop' ...)`. On Autumn billing accounts no seats are released or refunded, so the never-connected inboxes stay granted and billed after the order terminalizes.

The upstream contributing cause is that the pipeline assigns mailboxes to a paying order without checking that they are free at the provider.

## Blast radius

122 inboxes across 11 organizations on 15 orders share the `account_exists` connect signature (max retry_count 25, earliest inbox row 2026-03-05, most recent 2026-08-27). 81 of those inboxes sit on 8 orders still in `requires_attention` with `completed_at` null; 41 sit on 7 orders already `completed` (3 organizations), where the seats remain billed after finalization; 20 are at or above the 24-attempt cap. Query: `SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT organization_id), max(retry_count), min(created_at), max(created_at) FROM mail_inbox WHERE status='error' AND connection_error LIKE '%account_exists%'`, counted 2026-09-23. Confirmed affected: 11 organizations. Not settled: the population that traversed the path without confirmed failure (every pre-warmed order that assigned a mailbox already claimed at the provider), because no query separates it.

## Proposed fix

A mailbox that the provider reports as already owned elsewhere is a permanent conflict: detect it at connect time, stop retrying it, and surface it as a terminal, operator-visible failure instead of burning the retry budget. When an order is finalized with unconnected inboxes, release or refund those seats for every billing provider, not only Whop. Prevent the conflict upstream by not assigning a mailbox that is already claimed at the provider.

## What's included

Detecting the permanent conflict as non-retryable, terminal finalization that releases unconnected seats on Autumn, and a provider-availability check before assignment. Not included: reclaiming a mailbox from the workspace that already holds it, and the general billing reconciliation between supplier inventory and customer entitlements, which belongs to the existing billing-drift master.

## Regression seam

Entry: a pre-warmed order whose mailbox the provider reports as already owned by another workspace. Observable red-before behavior: the reconcile loop keeps re-invoking the connect until `MAX_INBOX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS` is exhausted, then finalizes with the seats still granted. Green-after: the permanent conflict is classified immediately and the unconnected seats are released or refunded at finalization for an Autumn account. A test at `finalizeUnfulfillableOrderAfterRetries` and one at the connect-result handling in the provider-agnostic path prove it.

## Done when

* A provider-reported `account_exists` conflict stops being retried rather than consuming the 24-attempt budget.
* Finalizing an order with unconnected inboxes releases or refunds those seats on an Autumn billing account, and the granted-seat count on the billing account matches the number of connected inboxes.
* A regression test proves the causal mechanism at the named seam.

## Reports

* ENG-14185

relatedSnapshot.title: NonRetriableError: Mailbox is not actively bound to a workspace its owner belongs to
DFY domain orders that fail leave names claimed and un-cancellable, blocking re-purchase and leaving the domain store inconsistent
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Root cause

When a Done-For-You domain order fails to provision at the provider, the domain rows are written to `mail_domain` (which has a global unique index `mail_domain_domain_unique` on `domain`) and left in a `failed` or `pending` state. Those rows are never released, so they keep holding the name for the original organization. A later order for the same name throws "Unable to claim domains for this organization" at the claim step, silently drops the overlapping domains, and leaves the new order stuck in `provisioning`.

Separately, a domain that failed still renders in Billing with no Cancel option, and the domain store availability check reads the registrar/provider (which never registered the failed name) instead of `mail_domain`. The result is a failed domain that shows as "available to purchase" while its name is actually still claimed internally.

## Evidence

* `apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/mail/process-create-order.ts` `processCreateColdMailOrder`: claims domains into `mail_domain` (unique on `domain`), throws "Unable to claim domains for this organization: ..." when a name is already held, and on provider failure writes domains to `status='failed'` with the order left `requires_attention` or `provisioning`.
* `apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/billing/reconcile-domain-orders-cron.ts`: retries failed inboxes on `requires_attention` orders, but does not release a domain name that failed at the provider and does not recover the duplicate-domain-claim collision.

## Blast radius (counted 2026-08-27)

Domain orders stuck in a non-terminal provisioning state: 17 `provisioning` across 17 organizations, 66 `requires_attention` across 66 organizations, 17 `failed` across 16 organizations. Done-For-You specifically: 3 `provisioning`, 26 `requires_attention`.

Domains in `failed` status with at least one `active` inbox (counted 2026-09-05): 106 domains across 41 organizations.

Paid `requires_attention` orders older than 7 days that hold `failed` domains (counted 2026-09-11): 26 orders across 25 organizations, holding 51 failed domains. Never-retried `error` inboxes on failed domains older than 7 days: 33, across 5 organizations. A 2026-09-10 count of the same cohort returned identical figures.

DFY orders stranded by a stale cross-organization `mail_domain` claim, with no saved provider order id and stale beyond 24 hours (counted 2026-09-23): 5 orders across 5 organizations and 5 users, from the ENG-14139 report. Collision cascade as of 2026-09-23: one stale failed claim is a foreign claim on 4 later DFY orders across 4 organizations, and pending claims written by two stuck orders block 4 further organizations' orders. The wider stuck-in-`provisioning` population is 9 orders across 9 organizations, of which 4 belong to ENG-13308's stall mechanism.

## Fix direction

* Release a failed domain's claim so the name can be re-purchased, and reconcile the domain store's availability check against owned-but-failed domains.
* Stop silently dropping overlapping domains from a new DFY order; fail fast with a clear message to the customer instead.

relatedSnapshot.title: Provisioned inboxes stuck in error despite order/diagnostics reporting them connected
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Customer report

```text
Workspace <workspace-slug> purchased 18 inboxes across 6 domains via provisioning order <uuid> (pre_warmed, paidAt 2026-01-25T15:40:44Z, completed step 6/6, provisioningLastUpdated 2026-01-26T06:26:48Z).

Live inbox health check (widget_inbox_health) shows all 18 of these accounts currently in "error" status (errorCode null, lastUsedAt null, warmupScore 100, warmupStatus 1 for each) — none ready.

The order's own diagnostics list every one of the 18 inboxes across all 6 domains as connected: true with no connectionError, and each domain status "success". But the same order's reconciliation block records inboxesActive: 0, inboxesConnected: 0, inboxesMissing: 18, inboxesCharged: 18 — directly contradicting the per-inbox diagnostic log.

No provisioning job failures were recorded in the last 7 days for this workspace.

This is a mismatch between what provisioning recorded (all inboxes connected) and both the live provider read (all in error) and the order's own reconciliation counters (0 active/connected, 18 missing), despite full charge. Customer has taken no incorrect action; this looks like a platform-side inconsistency in how inbox connection state is being recorded or synced after provisioning completes. Needs engineering to reconcile why diagnostics say connected while reconciliation and live status say otherwise, and why none of the 18 charged inboxes are actually active.
```

## Verified scope

* Workspace: Name 4's Workspace (<workspace-slug>)
* Organization ID: <uuid>
* Support conversation: <uuid>

relatedSnapshot.title: Customer report: 15 of 36 pre-warmed inboxes stuck in Error, Reconnect returns "Mailbox not found" and never clears the inbox
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Source

Intercom conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>

## Bounded conversation context

Customer reports (2026-09-21/22) that several mailboxes have shown an error and have not been sending for over a month; the count has grown from 6 to 15. He has opened several support tickets for the same issue over the past month or two without resolution. A frontline agent reactivated the inboxes on 2026-09-22 and it did not work. He asks for the 15 failing inboxes to be deleted and replaced with working ones and for one month of all 15 being down to be refunded / credited. Three screenshots of the Cold Email Agent email-accounts page were attached. Product area named on the conversation: Email accounts & domains.

## Testable claim

15 of the workspace's 36 pre-warmed sending inboxes are stuck in Error and have sent nothing because the Reconnect path asks the mail provider for a mailbox id it does not resolve, so the provider answers "Mailbox not found" and the inbox never returns to Active, leaving the workspace sending from only 21 inboxes.

## Current evidence

* Production: 33 mail_inbox rows for the workspace, 21 active/connected and 12 status=error, connected=false. The 12 carry three distinct connection errors: 6 "Mailbox OAuth connection threw an exception: Mailbox not found" with the stored provider id echoed in the message, 3 "Disconnected via Company Three account_error webhook", 3 "Waiting on zapmail oauth connection".
* Provider: the workspace sub-workspace holds all 36 sending accounts; exactly 15 report a failed status with autofix_failed, timestamped between 2026-08-19 and 2026-09-21. Three of those 15 have no local mail_inbox row at all, which is why the local count reads 12 and the customer's count of 15 is the accurate one.
* OAuth session history for the workspace: 16 failed sessions, all "Mailbox OAuth connection threw an exception: Mailbox not found" between 2026-09-19 and 2026-09-22; 50 expired sessions, including repeated "Waiting on zapmail oauth connection" for three inboxes from 2026-08-19/20/21; 30 completed sessions earlier in 2026.
* Sending: the 21 healthy inboxes are still sending; a healthy inbox in the same workspace sent mail on 2026-09-22, the day of the report. An inbox in the failed group last sent on 2026-08-12.
* Name 8: failed process-account-error-reconnect runs in the last week, with the invoke-connect-oauth step failing.

## Suspected code path

* apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/campaign/workspaces/process-account-error-reconnect.ts (processAccountErrorReconnect) marks the inbox Error and invokes processConnectOAuth with mailboxId = the stored mail_inbox.provider_id.
* apps/web/trpc/routers/outreach/email-accounts.ts (triggerOAuthReconnect) sends mailboxId, orderId and domain as undefined for a customer-initiated Reconnect.
* apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/campaign/workspaces/process-connect-oauth.ts forwards that id to ColdMailReseller POST /mailboxes/oauth and records "Mailbox OAuth connection threw an exception: Mailbox not found. Context: mailboxId=<id>, email=<address>".
* apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/campaign/workspaces/poll-oauth-session.ts records "Waiting on zapmail oauth connection".

## Blast radius

Counted from production on 2026-09-24: 16,058 inboxes in Error across 1,167 organizations. Of those, 5,762 inboxes / 444 organizations carry the "Mailbox not found" reconnect error, 497 / 87 the account_error webhook state, and 339 / 174 the zapmail oauth class.

Customer reports (2026-09-22) that every pre-warmed inbox in the workspace shows an Error status, that reconnect attempts stay at "Reconnect in Progress" for over 48 hours, and that toggling an inbox to enabled briefly shows Active before it returns to Error. On 2026-09-23 she adds that her campaign stopped running and that she cannot start any new campaigns. Frontline agent reactivated the inboxes on 2026-09-22 and confirmed they still failed, then escalated to the tech team.

* Product area named on the conversation: Email accounts & domains
* Workspace: cold email agent email-accounts page, 15 pre-warmed inboxes across 5 domains (5 completed pre-warmed orders, all provisioned 2026-03-30)

## Testable claim

Every pre-warmed inbox in the workspace is in Error and cannot be reconnected: the Reconnect path sends a mailbox id ColdMailReseller does not resolve, so the provider answers "Mailbox not found" and the inbox never returns to Active, which leaves the workspace with no sending accounts and blocks campaign sending.

## Current evidence

* 15/15 mail_inbox rows status=error, connected=false; 14 carry "Disconnected via Company Three account_error webhook", 1 carries the "Mailbox not found" OAuth exception.
* 53 Company Three account_error webhook events between 2026-09-19T15:07Z and 2026-09-23T05:57Z for these accounts.
* 15 failed cea_oauth_sessions, each with "Mailbox OAuth connection threw an exception: Mailbox not found. Context: mailboxId=<stored provider_id>, email=<address>", between 2026-09-20 and 2026-09-22.
* Last email_sent webhook for the workspace: 2026-09-18T19:37Z. One campaign is still "active" with no sends; three campaigns sit in draft.
* Provider side: the corresponding Company Three accounts exist in the workspace sub-workspace and report warmup activity, so the durable failure is the Acquisity reconnect path, not a missing provider account.

## Suspected code path

* apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/campaign/workspaces/process-account-error-reconnect.ts (processAccountErrorReconnect) marks the inbox Error and invokes processConnectOAuth with mailboxId = stored mail_inbox.provider_id.
* apps/web/trpc/routers/outreach/email-accounts.ts (triggerOAuthReconnect) sends mailboxId: undefined for a customer-initiated Reconnect.
* apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/campaign/workspaces/process-connect-oauth.ts forwards that id to ColdMailReseller POST /mailboxes/oauth.

relatedSnapshot.title: Restore CRM email for mailboxes left without a workspace binding
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Since 04 September, almost every rep with a connected Gmail or Outlook mailbox has been unable to send, reply to, draft or schedule email from the CRM, and their mailbox has stopped syncing. They see "Email account is not bound to this organization". This restores it by filling in the missing workspace record for every mailbox we can resolve from existing data, and by setting Name 11's mailbox to AI Acquisition LT.

Reported by Name 11 in #crm-feedback on 07 September: Slack message.

## Problem

ENG-13437 (Acquisity/Acquisity#6258) introduced a record saying which workspace each connected mailbox belongs to. It created that record as an empty table and shipped a manual script to fill it in for mailboxes that already existed. ENG-13439 (Acquisity/Acquisity#6260) then started requiring that record for both Gmail and Outlook, five hours later on the same day. PR 6258 set out a gate that had to be cleared first, ending in "confirm zero connected mailboxes remain without an active binding". The gate was not cleared, so the requirement went live against an almost empty table.

Counted against production on 07 September: 3,808 connected Gmail and Outlook mailboxes, 19 with a workspace record, and 3,789 without. All 19 were created on 04, 05 and 06 September, which is the pattern of people connecting a mailbox after the deploy rather than of a fill-in run.

Nobody on the team has shell access to production, so the fill-in cannot be run by hand. It has to ship as a change that runs itself on deploy.

## Proposed fix

Fill in the missing workspace record on deploy, using the same rules the existing script already uses. A mailbox that has only ever been used in one workspace is assigned to that workspace. A mailbox with no usage history whose owner belongs to exactly one workspace is assigned to that workspace. Anything else is left alone rather than guessed at. Name 11's mailbox is set to AI Acquisition LT explicitly, because his has been used in two workspaces and the rules would otherwise skip it.

## What's included

Included: the automatic fill-in for every mailbox the rules can resolve, roughly 3,277 of the 3,789, plus an explicit assignment for Name 11's mailbox. Re-running it must change nothing.

Deliberately excluded: the roughly 511 mailboxes the rules cannot resolve. Those stay blocked after this ships and are covered under Expected outcome and Open questions. Also excluded: any change to how connecting, disconnecting or reconnecting a mailbox behaves, and any change to the workspace requirement itself.

Name 12's assignment depends on James confirming AI Acquisition LT, which he has done.

## How it should work

Resolution runs in this order for each connected Gmail or Outlook mailbox that has no workspace record at all:

* If the mailbox has calendar or recording history in exactly one workspace, use that workspace.
* If it has history in more than one, leave it alone.
* Otherwise, if its owner belongs to exactly one live workspace, use that workspace.
* Otherwise, leave it alone.

A mailbox that already has a record, active or not, is never touched, so a mailbox somebody deliberately disconnected is not silently reconnected. The fill-in is safe to run more than once and must not fail the deploy if someone connects a mailbox at the same moment.

Name 11's mailbox (`<uuid>`) is assigned to AI Acquisition LT (`<uuid>`). His existing calendar and recording history stays where it is; the record only governs where his mailbox may send and sync from now on.

## Who can do what

No permission model changes. The workspace requirement introduced by ENG-13437, ENG-13438 and ENG-13439 stays exactly as it is: a mailbox recorded against workspace A is still refused when someone tries to use it from workspace B, and the mailbox owner still has to be a live member of the workspace being written into.

## What the user sees

Reps whose mailbox is resolved stop seeing "Email account is not bound to this organization" after the deploy, and sending, replying, drafting, scheduling and inbox sync work again with nothing for them to do. Name 12 sees the same, in AI Acquisition LT. Reps whose mailbox cannot be resolved keep seeing the same message until the follow-up work lands.

## Done when

* Every connected Gmail or Outlook mailbox that the rules can resolve has an active workspace record after deploy.
* Name 11's mailbox is recorded against AI Acquisition LT and he can send, reply, draft and schedule CRM email again.
* A mailbox recorded against one workspace is still refused when used from another.
* A mailbox that already had a record, active or not, is unchanged.
* Running the fill-in a second time changes nothing and does not fail.

## Open questions

The roughly 511 mailboxes the rules cannot resolve need a decision, with these numbers: 248 owners belong to several workspaces and the mailbox has no usage history to break the tie, 191 have usage history in more than one workspace, and 72 have owners who belong to no workspace at all. The last 72 were already refused before 04 September, so they are not a regression; the other 439 are.

Recommended default: a follow-up change so that a mailbox with no record at all falls back to the membership check that applied before 04 September, rather than being refused. That clears all 439 at once and needs no input from anyone. Two alternatives, if a stricter answer is wanted: bind the 178 of the 191 that have one clearly dominant workspace, or ask those reps to disconnect and reconnect the mailbox from the workspace they want it tied to.

## Expected outcome

3,278 mailboxes work again on deploy, including Name 12's. 511 remain blocked pending the follow-up decision above, of which 439 are people who could send email before 04 September and currently cannot.

## Implementation context

Production counts, the exact refusing code paths, the resolution rules, the concurrency guard the migration needs, and the test seams are captured in AI context.md.

relatedSnapshot.title: Stop stale mailbox runs from scheduling Recall bots
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

A disconnected, reconnected, or unauthorized mailbox cannot schedule or update a Recall bot from stale work.

## Problem

Mailbox authorization can change while a provider request is in flight.

## Proposed fix

Carry the exact mailbox generation through bot creation and schedule updates, rechecking it before and after provider calls.

## What's included

Bot creation, schedule updates, binding checks, provider compensation, and race tests.

Excluded: cancellation behavior and durable rate-limit retries owned by Retry rate-limited bot scheduling before the meeting.

## Blocked by

* Prevent obsolete Recall bot webhooks from changing the current recording.

## How it should work

Authorization is checked before contacting Recall. Provider success is checked again before persistence. If disconnect, reconnect, membership removal, or another generation change makes the run stale, no bot is adopted and any provider success is sent to durable cleanup.

## Who can do what

This is background behavior. It preserves mailbox ownership, workspace membership, organization boundaries, and the existing SCA Live Connect feature gate.

## What the user sees

No new interface. Stale calendar work cannot deploy or reschedule a recording bot after mailbox access changes.

## Done when

- [ ] Authorization is checked before contacting Recall.
- [ ] Provider success is checked again before persistence.
- [ ] A stale success is sent to durable cleanup.
- [ ] Membership removal, disconnect, or generation change prevents persistence.
- [ ] Race tests cover authorization changing in both directions.

## Open questions

None: all required decisions are settled.

## Expected outcome

Only work authorized by the mailbox's current workspace generation can schedule or update its Recall bot.

## Implementation context

Detailed source evidence, constraints, and test seams are in AI context.md.
